938: 4.5. A minimality conjecture
939: As we shall see in a moment,
940: our generators for I_{w} are not minimal. However,
941: we believe the following holds:
942: Conjecture 4.10 .
943: The two generating sets for the ideal J_{v_{r,s,t,n}} given in Theorem 4.8
944: are both minimal.
945: Via computer, we have verified this conjecture for all bigrassmannian permutations
946: where r\leq 4 and n-r\leq 5.
947: In fact, Conjecture 4.10 indicates obstructions to short presentations of
948: H^{\star}(X_{w}) in general. We now give
949: a family of ideals that would require a large number of generators if the conjecture is true.
950: For a positive integer m, let n=4m, and consider in
951: W=S_{n}=S_{4m} the bigrassmannian v_{r,s,t,n} that corresponds
952: to r=n-r=2m and i=j=m. Then a=b=m, and J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}(=I_{w_{r,s,t,n}}) requires
953: (4.9)
954: \binom{2m}{m}\sim\frac{4^{m}}{\sqrt{\pi m}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}^{n+2}}{\sqrt{\pi n}}
955: generators according to Conjecture 4.10 .
956: The size of any minimal generating set of a homogeneous ideal is
957: well-defined. This is implied by the following well-known fact:
958: Proposition 4.11 .
959: Let R be a commutative ring, and \Lambda=\oplus_{n\geq 0}\Lambda_{n} a graded, connected R-algebra, meaning that \Lambda_{0}=R and \Lambda_{i}\Lambda_{j}\subset\Lambda_{i+j}. Let M be a
960: graded \Lambda-module, with degrees bounded below, meaning that
961: M=\oplus_{n\geq N}M_{n} for some N\in{\mathbb{Z}}, and \Lambda_{i}M_{j}\subset M_{i+j}.
962: Then a set of homogeneous elements \{m_{i}\}_{i=1}^{t} generate M as a \Lambda-module
963: if and only if their images \{\bar{m_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{t} span M/\Lambda_{+}M as a R-module.
964: In particular, \{m_{i}\}_{i=1}^{t} form a minimal \Lambda-generating set with respect to
965: inclusion for M if and only if \{\bar{m_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{t} form a minimal R-spanning
966: set for M/\Lambda_{+}M.
967: In our setting, the well-definedness follows by setting
968: \Lambda=\oplus_{n\geq 0}\Lambda_{n} to be the graded ring of
969: symmetric functions with {\mathbb{Z}} coefficients and setting
970: M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}, so that the {\mathbb{Z}}-module M/\Lambda_{+}M
971: is a finitely generated abelian group.
972: Thus we conjecture that this abelian group M/\Lambda_{+}M requires
973: \binom{a+b}{a} generators, and in fact, we suspect that
974: M/\Lambda_{+}M\cong{\mathbb{Z}}^{\binom{a+b}{a}}. So far a proof
975: has eluded us.

groundings.excerpt:
Presenting the cohomology of a Schubert variety: Proof of the minimality conjecture
Abstract A minimal presentation of the cohomology ring of the flag manifold was given in A. Borel (1953). This presentation was extended by E. Akyildiz–A. Lascoux–P. Pragacz (1992) to a nonminimal one for all Schubert varieties. Work of V. Gasharov–V. Reiner (2002) gave a short, that is, polynomial‐size, presentation for a subclass of Schubert varieties that includes the smooth ones. In V. Reiner–A. Woo–A. Yong (2011), a general shortening was found; it implies an exponential upper bound of on the number of generators required. That work states a minimality conjecture whose significance would be an exponential lower bound of on the number of generators needed in worst case, giving the first obstructions to short presentations. We prove the minimality conjecture. Our proof uses the Hopf algebra structure of the ring of symmetric functions.
